title: Constructor functions
learningObjectives: Explain constructor functions and choose suitable object-oriented patterns.

understand.concept: A constructor function is traditionally called with new to create an object whose prototype is set to the constructor's prototype. The constructor can initialise instance properties using this. Calling a constructor without new can produce different or erroneous behaviour.
understand.whyItMatters: Constructor functions appear in existing JavaScript code and explain how many built-in objects are structured. Modern class syntax provides a clearer surface over prototype-based construction.
understand.analogy: A constructor is a reusable plan that initialises each new object and links it to shared methods.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript object identity, prototypes, and class semantics are defined by the language.

explain.narrative: new creates an instance, binds this to it, and connects it to Course.prototype. The describe method is shared through the prototype.

examples.explanation: new creates an instance, binds this to it, and connects it to Course.prototype. The describe method is shared through the prototype.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the object creation or class behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Create two instances from a constructor and verify they share the same prototype method but have different title values.
practise.independentTask: Model a small domain using the simplest suitable object pattern. Explain the trade-offs between plain objects, functions, prototypes, and classes.
hints: Separate instance data from shared behaviour.
Check own properties and inherited properties.
Prefer composition when capabilities need to vary independently.

questions.prompt: Where are methods commonly placed to be shared by instances created with a constructor function?
questions.explanation: Instances inherit methods placed on the constructor function's prototype.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between a plain object, function, and class?
options: The actual data and behaviour requirements
A rule that every object must be a class
The number of lines in the file name
questions.answer: The actual data and behaviour requirements
questions.explanation: Choose the least complex abstraction that clearly expresses the required behaviour.
